title: SummitAI renewal & multi-region capacity extension review
summary: Quarterly renewal + expansion checkpoint. Customer requests additional Dedicated capacity and APAC region onboarding; negotiating a 12- to 24-month contract extension with minor pricing change tied to reserved commit. Discussed throughput targets, latency SLOs, private VPC option for sensitive workloads, SOC2 and KMS requirements. Agreed next steps: Redwood to share updated quote and contract markups, SE to run a short benchmarking run in Redwood Dedicated with their peak prompt set, procurement to confirm PO timeline.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-03-30 15:00 PT | Duration: 48m | Attendees: Maya Chen, Daniel Park (Redwood); Lena Ortiz, Tom Reynolds, Priya Kapoor (SummitAI)

[00:00] Maya Chen: hi everyone, thanks for joining. this is Maya from Redwood, i'm the AE on your account. we also have Daniel, our senior SE. how's it going Lena?
[00:10] Lena Ortiz: hey Maya, good, thanks. busy week but glad we're on.
[00:14] Tom Reynolds: yeah, morning all, quick heads up — Priya's on deck for procurement items later.
[00:19] Priya Kapoor: hi all, thanks — i'll listen in and flag timeline stuff.

[00:30] Maya Chen: quick agenda — renewal timing, capacity bump for Q3, APAC region onboarding, and any contractual/legal asks. want to keep it pragmatic.
[00:38] Lena Ortiz: sounds good. to frame — our usage has grown ~2.6x year over year, peak inference loads hit about 1.2M tokens/day across several microservices. current Dedicated pool is fine for US but we need predictable latency in APAC and want a committed plan.
[00:55] Daniel Park: thanks, that aligns w/ what we saw in telemetry. do you have target p95 latency for your customer-facing endpoints?
[01:01] Lena Ortiz: we try to keep p95 under 250ms for short-form prompts, ideally under 200ms. for larger chat flows maybe 350ms is ok.
[01:09] Daniel Park: ok. in Redwood Dedicated with appropriate instance sizing and prefix KV cache you should be able to hit sub-200 for 90% of requests. the tricky bit is cross-region replication — if we serve from US region to APAC you'll see added RTT. that's why we recommend APAC co-located Dedicated pools or our Hosted APAC endpoint as a stopgap.

[01:40] Tom Reynolds: what's the difference cost-wise? we were looking at a small 3-GPU Dedicated pool in APAC vs using Hosted routing.
[01:47] Maya Chen: great question. rough rule: Hosted APAC incurs per-token usage fees and egress routing but has no upfront commit; Dedicated APAC is reserved capacity — higher committed cost but predictable unit economics and isolation. We'll send a detailed delta in the quote.
[02:05] Lena Ortiz: procurement will care about committed spend. Priya, what's your threshold for a reserved contract?
[02:10] Priya Kapoor: for CAPEX planning we prefer annual commitments with options to scale; 12 months is doable, 24 months better for discounting but needs legal review. also we'll need standard MSA + DPA and vendor security pack.

[02:30] Daniel Park: noted. on the technical side, if you go Dedicated in APAC we can place your model variants there; we support quantized model runtimes which reduce GPU memory and improve throughput. do you want us to run a bench with your prompt set?
[02:44] Lena Ortiz: yes — we have a canonical prompt set and a few long-context flows. can you model token distribution? our tail latency has been the pain point.
[02:52] Daniel Park: absolutely. SE suggestion: we run a short 24-hour benchmark simulating peak QPS using your prompt set, include prefix caching scenarios, and measure p50/p95/p99 and token cost. we'll need an API key and sample prompts.

[03:10] Tom Reynolds: data residency — some of our customers in Japan require data to stay in-region for the inference request logs for 30 days. can we do that?
[03:17] Maya Chen: yes, APAC Dedicated can be configured with local retention; for Hosted we have region-scoped endpoints but logs might be centralized unless you opt into our Private deployment model. for strict residency and auditability, Redwood Private (VPC) or on-prem package is the path.

[03:35] Priya Kapoor: ok, legal will want SOC 2 details, SAML SSO integrations, and KMS key ownership options. we prefer customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest.
[03:44] Maya Chen: we support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM integrations and SSO via SAML/Okta. SOC 2 Type II report and ISO docs are in the security portal — we'll share the package.

[04:00] Speaker 1: (murmur) and audit logging — retention?
[04:04] Daniel Park: audit logs can be exported to your SIEM or to an S3 bucket in-region; retention is adjustable and configurable per account.

[04:18] Lena Ortiz: about pricing — our CFO would like to see projected unit cost after adding APAC and the reserved commit. Any estimate?
[04:25] Maya Chen: we'll produce a delta cost model: current unit price, projected with APAC Dedicated at X GPUs, and the discount tier for 12 vs 24 months. expect about 12-18% discount for 24-month heavy commit; exact depends on GPU class and sustained throughput.

[04:45] Tom Reynolds: how do rollouts and fallbacks work if APAC pool is temporarily saturated? we can't degrade user experiences.
[04:52] Daniel Park: Redwood supports routing policies: canary, A/B and automated fallback to cross-region or to hosted variants. you can set latency-first or cost-first policies. also autoscaling burst helps absorb short spikes.

[05:10] Priya Kapoor: procurement: timeline — if we sign within 2 weeks can we have APAC capacity provisioned by mid-Q2?
[05:17] Maya Chen: provisioning depends on GPU availability in region; typical lead time 2-4 weeks for Dedicated. we'll prioritize SummitAI as you are renewing.

[05:28] Lena Ortiz: there's also a question from engineering — model version pinning and rollbacks. we want to be able to pin to a specific model artifact and rollback if quality regresses.
[05:36] Daniel Park: supported — model versioning and canary rollout with automatic fallback and compare metrics. we also offer eval hooks for quality regression detection tied to your test prompts.

[05:50] Tom Reynolds: any concerns about tokenization differences across models? we rely on consistent embeddings for semantic search.
[05:55] Daniel Park: we'll surface model family compatibility and embedding stable variants; when switching models embedding drift is a risk — we'll run a small embedding drift analysis during the bench.

[06:08] Lena Ortiz: security caveat: some of our legal team wants Redwood under the vendor DPA with subprocessor list.
[06:13] Maya Chen: yes, DPA and subprocessor list are standard; we maintain a changelog and can provide updates.

[06:22] Priya Kapoor: good. procurement also wants a sample SOW for the Dedicated onboarding and runbook.
[06:28] Maya Chen: we'll include a short SOW in the contract package — provisioning, runbook for failover, and a 2-week ramp support included.

[06:40] Lena Ortiz: about the bench — can you measure cost per generated token for our long-form chat flows? we need that to present to the board.
[06:48] Daniel Park: yes, bench will report cost per 1k tokens across model and quantization configs, and show tradeoffs for latency vs cost.

[07:00] Maya Chen: ok let's talk numbers high-level so we can get the quote ready. current commit is 12k GPU-hours/month?
[07:07] Lena Ortiz: roughly, yes — currently on 8-GPU pool with mixed usage.
[07:12] Maya Chen: for APAC we recommend starting with 3x A100-equivalent GPUs for the Dedicated pool and test. that should cover your expected Q3 peak with auto-burst configured. price wise — we'll send variants but plan on roughly +35% on top of current monthly committed spend for the regional pool before discounts.

[07:35] Tom Reynolds: is the +35% assuming same model families and quantization?
[07:38] Daniel Park: yes. if you move to more aggressive quantization or smaller model variants, cost drops further but quality needs to be validated.

[07:50] Lena Ortiz: legal/term ask — our legal prefers a 12-month extension with a 60-day exit for severe SLA breaches. willing to consider 24 months if the price improves.
[07:59] Maya Chen: understood. we can propose 12 months default, with a 24-month term as an alternate with better pricing and potentially a service credit SLAs addendum.

[08:12] Priya Kapoor: on billing — do you support consolidated billing and monthly invoices with PO?
[08:17] Maya Chen: yes we do consolidated billing, monthly invoicing; many enterprise customers use PO+net30. We'll coordinate with your finance team.

[08:28] Speaker 2: (background) question about private deployment costs
[08:31] Maya Chen: private deployments (VPC/on-prem) are licensed differently — platform fee + infra costs; it's typically a larger initial commitment and used when residency or audit controls are mandatory.

[08:44] Tom Reynolds: our immediate priority is predictable latency for APAC and better unit economics. private deployment is a future conversation.

[08:55] Daniel Park: action item for SE: we'll need a sanitized prompt sample, expected qps, and desired p95 target. we'll run bench for 24-72 hours, share results.

[09:05] Lena Ortiz: timeframe — can bench be done this week? we can scrub and share samples today.
[09:09] Daniel Park: yes we can kick off once we have the sample and an API key; expecting 48 hours to get initial results.

[09:18] Maya Chen: procurement next steps — Priya, can you share target approval date?
[09:22] Priya Kapoor: tentatively 2026-04-16 for PO approval; legal may need a week to review the MSA after we get the redlines.

[09:31] Maya Chen: great. i'll get pricing and contract options over by Friday, 2026-04-02.

[09:36] Tom Reynolds: one more ops question — how does autoscaling billing work? if we burst above committed capacity for short periods, how is that charged?
[09:43] Daniel Park: bursts are billed at pay-as-you-go rates; you can cap burst usage or set alerts. billing shows committed vs burst usage separately so you can track overages.

[09:55] Lena Ortiz: can you also include a comparison of hosting APAC on Redwood Hosted vs spinning Dedicated vs Private? a quick 1-pager would help the execs.
[10:04] Maya Chen: yes, we'll include a decision matrix: cost, latency, compliance, time-to-provision.

[10:12] Priya Kapoor: procurement needs a contract contact and legal PO template from Redwood.
[10:17] Maya Chen: i'll attach both.

[10:22] Speaker 1: small aside — any competitors mentioned in vendor reviews?
[10:26] Lena Ortiz: we've looked at FastServe AI and CloudForge's managed endpoints; FastServe had lower latencies historically but higher cost.

[10:34] Maya Chen: thanks — helpful context.

[10:38] Daniel Park: quick note about KV cache — in transcripts sometimes clients call it K V cache and we see mismatches in logs; we'll align the nomenclature in the runbook.

[10:48] Lena Ortiz: the team will also want a short playbook for rollback and incident response if APAC is down.

[10:53] Daniel Park: we'll provide a runbook with failover steps: route to US, degrade gracefully, and telemetry alerts thresholds.

[11:02] Maya Chen: ok let's do a recap and assign owners.
[11:06] Maya Chen: recap: Redwood to send updated quote and two term options (12/24 mo), SE to run benchmark with SummitAI prompt set, security pack and SOC2 docs to be shared, SOW/runbook + contract templates attached.

[11:20] Priya Kapoor: sounds right. timeline recap: bench kick-off ASAP, pricing & contract by 2026-04-02, PO target 2026-04-16.

[11:32] Lena Ortiz: thanks everyone.
[11:34] Tom Reynolds: thanks, bye.
[11:35] Maya Chen: thanks all — we'll follow up in email with artifacts. bye.

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcript with a few mis-hearings and short filler words.
